🔢 How to read the UMF number

UMF stands for Unique Manuka Factor, a grading system awarded by the UMFHA after testing in accredited laboratories. It confirms the honey is genuine Manuka and measures its natural signature markers, including MGO (methylglyoxal). The higher the number, the higher the grade, so the 15+ jar is graded above the 10+ jar.

🌿 Where it comes from

Bees gather nectar from the flowers of the Manuka shrub, which grows in New Zealand. Because Manuka fraud is common worldwide, the UMFHA was set up with New Zealand government support to protect genuine producers.

Bees make this honey from the nectar of the Manuka shrub that grows in New Zealand, which is why it tastes different from ordinary blossom honey: darker and thicker. It reaches us in its sealed jar as packed.

🔢 How to read UMF and MGO on the label

  1. UMF 10+: Unique Manuka Factor, a grade set by the UMFHA association in New Zealand. Honey carrying it is tested in laboratories the association approves.
  2. MGO 300+: methylglyoxal, a naturally occurring compound typical of Manuka, with its figure printed on the jar.
  3. Read both numbers together when buying, as they tell you more than either one alone.

It is a grade on the UMFHA association scale in New Zealand. A higher number means a higher grade, and usually a deeper, denser taste.

📚 How is Manuka honey graded?

UMF stands for Unique Manuka Factor, a scale used to determine the grade of Manuka honey. The UMF Honey Association of New Zealand is the officially recognized body for testing and grading honey to strict standards, and honey that carries the UMF grading is tested in laboratories accredited by the association.

Another number that appears on Manuka jars is MGO, short for Methylglyoxal, a natural compound considered the main component of Manuka honey. The rule is easy to remember: a higher number means a higher grade, and the easiest way is to compare our four grades by UMF grade, which is 20+ in this jar.

📛 Why is it called Black Seed honey?

Because the bees visit the blossoms of this plant and gather their nectar, so the honey takes the name of the plant it came from, just as Sidr honey takes the name of the Sidr tree. This makes it a kind of its own among the kinds of honey.

🍽️ Serving it at home

🌙 EveningWarm tea sweetened with honey instead of sugar.
👥 GuestsA small dish next to the coffee and dates.
🎁 GiftsDivide part of it into small jars as gifts for your relatives.

🧊 If it crystallizes

Natural honey may crystallize over time, and this is normal. Place the jar in warm, not boiling, water and stir it from time to time until it becomes liquid again.
